content: Add an expert-skills layer under agent/skills/ as load-on-demand procedural playbooks, with the same machine enforcement as every other record layer.

Skills are a fourth record type beside experience and templates: experience holds validated observations about the world, templates hold passive record shapes, skills hold sequenced procedures whose correctness is enforced by repository machinery. Form: one directory per durable lowercase slug with a SKILL.md carrying name/description/status frontmatter; statuses Draft/Active/Retired; slugs never renamed after links exist.

The validator enforces the skill form: the skills README must index every skill directory in both directions, directory names must be slugs, and every skill needs a SKILL.md with non-empty name/description/status frontmatter. An absent skills directory stays valid so the layer remains optional until used.

Seeded three skills encoding procedures proven across this session series: add-component (registration through metaflux_add_component, role whitelist, nix filesets, component-graph verification), close-decision (ledger row to decisions-index with partial-closure handling), and record-session (scaffold through checkpoint).

Validator self-test extended to twenty cases; one vacuous-pass trap was caught during design: a missing-SKILL.md case would have tested a nonexistent directory instead, so the case keeps the directory physically present via a placeholder file. Repository validation initially failed on three link errors: two over-deep SKILL.md links (skills sits one level shallower than sessions) and one link to agent/templates/README.md, which had never existed — the template index was written as part of this change.
Final verification: self-test 20/20, repository validation ok (5 sessions, 50 events, 68 Markdown), dev preset 16/16.
